figures.quoteEnd: The frame capture is invisible inside the final product.
figures.essayAnchorEnd: The frame capture is invisible inside the final product.

audienceParagraphs.he: **Frame capture.** The model's definition of productivity becomes the memo's definition. Later drafts improve the prose inside the wrong boundary.
audienceParagraphs.k12: **Frame capture.** The model's standard of success becomes the student's. Her revisions polish the essay inside a boundary she never chose.

figures.quoteStart: Fluency substitution is easier to miss.
figures.quoteEnd: A paragraph that balances every consideration may never identify which risk actually matters most.
figures.essayAnchorEnd: may never identify which risk actually matters most.

audienceParagraphs.he: **Fluency substitution.** The balanced paragraph sounds like judgment. It weighs every study and never decides which one this firm should care about most.
audienceParagraphs.k12: **Fluency substitution.** "Mixed but largely successful" sounds like a historian weighing evidence. It weighs everything and commits to nothing a reader could argue with.

figures.quoteEnd: The student has bypassed the developmental struggle of forming a mental map and inherited one instead.
figures.essayAnchorEnd: forming a mental map and inherited one instead.

audienceParagraphs.he: **Premature synthesis.** The model connected three studies before the student knew enough about their designs to see that they measured different things in different workforces.

figures.quoteEnd: Appropriate reliance requires the student to identify which part of the task they are delegating, what evidence would justify that delegation, and what independent checks are required before discovering the error downstream.
The student believes they are working; the model has already done the framing.
figures.essayAnchorEnd: the model has already done the framing.

audienceParagraphs.he: **Invisible delegation.** "Summarize the research" handed over the criterion. The student believed she was asking for help with reading. She was also asking the model to decide what counted.
audienceParagraphs.k12: **Invisible delegation.** "Write an essay" handed over the most important decision in the assignment, which is what success should mean. The student thought she was asking for help writing.

figures.quoteStart: Institutional monoculture is the class-level version
figures.quoteEnd: the seminar is meant to develop.
figures.essayAnchorEnd: the range of strategic imagination the seminar is meant to develop.

audienceParagraphs.he: **Institutional monoculture.** Give the same assignment to thirty students using similar tools and similar prompts, and many will turn in some version of "the evidence is mixed; hybrid is the balance." The memos will differ in structure and sources while sharing one framing of the question. A seminar that should surface competing frames ends up comparing phrasings of a single one ([Deng, Brucks & Toubia, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20408)).
audienceParagraphs.k12: **Institutional monoculture.** Thirty students with similar tools will turn in many versions of "mixed but largely successful." The essays will differ in their examples and share one standard. A class discussion meant to surface competing arguments will mostly compare wording.

figures.quoteStart: Responsibility laundering is the final danger.
figures.quoteEnd: the question of who chose the frame does not have a satisfying answer.
